label: prop:frobenius-s-classification
title: Frobenius S-eigenvalue classification of the 3-term mass formula
html:
Under the Frobenius--Hopf antipode S \colon \sigma \leftrightarrow \sigma^{-1} on the Hecke algebra H_n(R, q), the three log-functionals in the Wedderburn mass formula (Wedderburn mass formula) carry exactly the following S-eigenvalues:

See Table 1.

Together with the S-classification of every coefficient in the formula:

See Table 2.

Term by term, the binding correction \alpha\bigl(\Phi_1 - 2[3]_q\,\Phi_2 + h_{\mathrm{A}}^2\,\Phi_3\bigr) decomposes as:

\begin{aligned}
\text{Term 1: } & \underbrace{1}_{+1} \cdot \underbrace{\Phi_1}_{+1} = +1 & \text{(\(S\)-even)} \\
\text{Term 2: } & \underbrace{-2[3]_q}_{+1} \cdot \underbrace{\Phi_2}_{+1} = +1 & \text{(\(S\)-even)} \\
\text{Term 3: } & \underbrace{h_{\mathrm{A}}^2}_{+1} \cdot \underbrace{\Phi_3}_{-1} = -1 & \text{(\(S\)-odd)}
\end{aligned}

Exactly one of the three terms is S-anti-invariant, namely the chirality term h_{\mathrm{A}}^2 \Phi_3. Consequently, any S-symmetric ansatz for the binding correction (such as the 2-term \alpha-blend \alpha V_{\mathrm{Frob}} + (1-\alpha) V_{\det}) necessarily lives in the 2-dimensional S-invariant subspace and cannot capture chirality regardless of the mixing parameter.
